title: Fast Plans, Faithful Actions: Closing the Planning-Execution Gap in Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Models
models: hierarchical waypoint VLA derived from pi0.5: PaliGemma (SigLIP + Gemma-2B) planner emitting waypoint tokens, 300M Gemma flow-matching action expert as executor, LoRA-adapted from released pi0.5 weights
action_head: flow/diffusion action expert (conditioned on discrete waypoint tokens generated by the VLM planner)
methods: token-level vs waypoint-block autoregressive plan decoding (Token-AR vs Block-AR)
controlled interventions with inputs and flow noise fixed: endpoint erasure, duration +4 steps, camera swap, instruction swap; sensitivity S relative to noise-resampling baseline
closed-loop utility U = success drop after erasing all plan endpoints
normalized goal modulation (NGM): goal displacement injected into every expert layer via AdaRMS with phase gate, condition noise and dropout
question: In a hierarchical pi0.5-style VLA, does the low-level action expert actually use the planner's waypoints, and can the interface be made both fast and faithful?
key_findings: With standard suffix-token conditioning, erasing the planned endpoint changes actions by only 0.6% of the change from resampling flow noise, while swapping the camera image changes them by 281% and swapping the instruction by 158%; duration +4 steps changes them by 19% (Sec. 6.3, Table 4).
Closed-loop: erasing every spatial endpoint costs nothing (U = 0.0 pp) on LIBERO-Long, so the executor ignores the plan's spatial content.

Naive deep goal injection overshoots: endpoint sensitivity 348%, image sensitivity falls to 27% of baseline, success drops to 15% (all timeouts) - a 'displacement-integrator shortcut' where the expert integrates the goal displacement instead of looking at images.
NGM (gated, noised, dropped-out goal route): endpoint sensitivity 42.6%, image response retained at 82%, LIBERO-Long success 91.0% -> 96.2%, and endpoint erasure now costs 7.4 pp.
LIBERO four-suite average: Token-AR 96.70, Block-AR 95.85, Block-AR + NGM 98.45 (released pi0.5 reported 96.85) (Table 2, N = 500 per suite).
Block-AR cuts serial planner passes from 57 to 8 (LIBERO) and 120 to 8 (16-DoF robot); real-robot plan latency 1094 -> 125 ms, motion duty cycle 28.7% -> 65.6%.
Real dual-arm robot: 48/60 (Token-AR), 46/60 (Block-AR), 51/60 (Block-AR + NGM) successes over three tasks (Table 5).

evidence.setting: both (LIBERO simulation; real Rokae AR5-5 dual-arm robot)
benchmarks: 3 real bimanual tasks (pepper-banana placement, pepper swap, shelf placement)
evidence.scale: LIBERO: 500 episodes per suite (10 tasks x 50 initial states); sensitivity on 64 frozen segments; real: 20 trials per task per method, 154 demos collected (120 for training); each variant trained once
evidence.statistics: no: single training run per variant, no CIs; authors note one point = 5 of 500 episodes
evidence.baselines: Token-AR + suffix conditioning, Block-AR + suffix conditioning, naive goal injection, released pi0.5 (reported numbers)

causal_validation: Yes: interventions on the plan input with all other inputs and flow noise fixed, measured both as action change (relative to a noise-resampling baseline) and as closed-loop task utility after endpoint erasure; the fix (NGM) is validated by showing endpoint erasure now hurts success while image sensitivity is mostly retained.
closed_loop: Yes: utility U and success rates are closed-loop LIBERO rollouts; sensitivity S is measured on frozen segments (open-loop).
limitations_stated: Validated on one pi0.5-derived hierarchy; Block-AR assumes fixed-format plan token groups, NGM relies on the expert's AdaRMS conditioning.
Each variant trained once; no variability estimate across training runs.
Real robot: 3 tasks x 20 trials per method limits precision for small differences.
critique: Exemplary intervention design for the review: it pairs an open-loop sensitivity ratio (with a noise baseline) with a closed-loop erasure utility and a check that other inputs are still used, showing that high sensitivity alone can indicate a shortcut rather than faithful use.

Key finding that a flow-matching action expert can almost completely ignore an explicit intermediate plan when it also sees image and language KV, which parallels the reasoning-chain results (2603.12717, 2510.16281) but at the action-expert interface.
The hierarchy is the authors' own construction, not released pi0.5, so 'pi0.5 ignores plans' is not shown; it shows that this training recipe produces plan-ignoring experts.
Real-robot gains (51/60 vs 48/60) are within noise at n = 20 per task; the clear wins are latency and the LIBERO-Long faithfulness diagnostics.
Single seed per variant means the +5.2 point LIBERO-Long gain is not separable from training variance.
one_line: In a pi0.5-derived planner-executor VLA, erasing the planner's waypoint endpoints barely changes the flow-matching expert's actions or success, but routing a gated, noise-regularized goal signal into every expert layer makes the plan matter (erasure now costs 7.4 points) and raises LIBERO-Long success to 96.2%.
